Chronological

/kro-nuh-LOJ-i-kul/ — rhymes with biological · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Chronological means arranged in the order in which events occurred in time.

The curators arranged every exhibit in strict chronological order, so that each step down the corridor carries the visitor a few million years later than the last.

Worked Example

The historian organized the ancient manuscripts by the order they were written, from earliest to latest, so readers could trace the civilization's development step by step through time.

Chronological means arranged in the exact order events occurred in time. It's not just any organized arrangement (that could be by size, alphabet, color, etc.); it's specifically organized by time order. The manuscripts from earliest to latest is the definition of chronological.

How Chronological Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

sequential

sequential: ordered one after another, on any basis

consecutive

consecutive: unbroken succession, not necessarily by time

temporal

temporal: relating to time generally, not to ordering

Antonyms

random

random: having no order or pattern at all

scrambled

scrambled: deliberately mixed out of proper order

How Strong Is It? — jumbled → arranged → chronological

jumbled vs. chronological

jumbled vs. chronological: The band's old tour posters lay jumbled in a box — jumbled only tells you they are mixed up, a far weaker word than chronological, which names the exact year-by-year order a fan would hang them in.

arranged vs. chronological

arranged vs. chronological: Saying the scientist's lab notebook entries were arranged tells you someone imposed some order — by topic, by importance, by anything; chronological is stronger because it pins down the one specific order of time, from first experiment to most recent.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — chrono-

Root — chrono-: time (from Greek khronos; the linking -o- glues the Greek pieces together)

Suffix — -log-

Suffix — -log-: account, study of (from Greek logos, 'word, reckoning')

Suffix — -ical

Suffix — -ical: relating to, characteristic of

Put it together

Put it together: Chrono- (time, from Greek khronos -- with the linking -o- that glues Greek pieces together) + -log- (account, study of, from Greek logos) + -ical (relating to) assembles the word in two steps: chronology is the account or ordering of time, and chronological means relating to that time-order -- arranged in the sequence events actually happened.

Use the root in a new word: anachronism

Use the root in a new word: anachronism: Having a character use a smartphone in a story set in 1952 is a clear anachronism that takes readers out of the story.

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Chronological is the precise term for arranging things in time order, especially in history, science, and literature. In everyday speech, say 'in order' or 'from beginning to end,' but chronological is the exact word when you want to emphasize arrangement by time.
